title: Critical theta-half Gibbs cancellation and local second-moment bound
question: At the critical fractional exponent theta=1/2, does the Gibbs relation exactly cancel the doubled-bond transition energy and reduce the Kubo-Mori shell to a local Gibbs second-moment bound?
promotion_boundary: R-371 proves and checks the critical theta-half Gibbs cancellation and a finite local Gibbs second-moment bound for the doubled-bond proxy. It does not prove a uniform second-moment estimate, common core, common alpha, KMS/GNS gap, continuum, or any QFT closure.
next_action: Prove a source-, volume- and cutoff-uniform local Gibbs second-moment estimate on a Hamiltonian-derived common core; then combine it with the R-371 identity and the R-370 low/high split for the direct D,delta-D corridor.
boundary: Finite actual-Q3 edge and square rows with all prefixes, translated bond terms, translated measured sites, orientations, signs, adjoints and beta values. The Gibbs state is the finite doubled local-bond proxy. Global KMS, common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS dynamics, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A and Pre-A remain open.
